learning_outcomes.text: At the end of the course, the student knows theoretical principles, functional schemes, methodologies for choice of components, design methods, optimization criteria both on technical and economic point of view, standards and rules regarding the mechanical plants which are auxiliary systems present in the production systems in order to make available the necessary services for the correct development of production processes.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical plants characterization. Technical-economical optimization methods.
Combined plants for production of heat and electric power.
Industrial steam production and distribution: steam generator operation, steam distribution networks, recovery and drain systems.
Multi-stage concentration plants for obtaining concentrated products of food industry. Concentration plants based on heat-pump principle.
Thermal plants using hot water for heat power necessities of industrial processes: functional schemes, pressurization methods, design criteria.
Thermal plants using hot air for drying processes of solid substances.

Plants for supply and distribution of industrial water. Pressurized and un-pressurized water storage tanks, water pressurization systems. Piping networks item: classification and selection of pipes, valves and coupling. Regulation, intercept and check valve operation. Open and close water network design.

Fire safety engineering. Hydrant and sprinkler plants design criteria. Automatic suppression fire plants (water, foam and gas extinguishers), portable equipments. Water mist fire plants. Fire alarm systems, fire alarm monitoring, smoke, heat & carbon monoxide detectors. Evacuation model simulation. Fire dynamic simulation.
Air conditioning plants for industrial and civil applications.
Refrigerating plants for industrial and civil applications. Estimate of cool load, isolant materials, refrigerating fluids. Refrigerating plants with one-stage ore two-stage compression.
Plants for production and distribution of compressed air : compressor system design, condensate drain systems, air network distribution.
teaching_methods: Theoretical lessons are completed by a series of exercises and applications to allow the student to be familiar with the common design practices

assessment_methods.method: Final exam (written test including theoretical and practical development of three arguments: two theoretical issues and a numeric-themed application)

assessment_rules: The final grade is assigned based on the overall assessment of the entire test. Higher grades are awarded for organic understanding, critical application ability, and clear/concise presentation, with attention to technical terms, graphs, and diagrams. A passing grade requires knowledge of key concepts, some critical application ability, and comprehensible technical language. A failing grade is given for knowledge gaps in key concepts, inappropriate language, or logic failures, or if at least one question is not sufficient.
